The Blockly editor with the Hello World script: the toolbox and its search, the blocks on the workspace, the trash can, the 3D text in the 3D view, Run The Code, the toolbox button and More, numbered as the tour explains them

Build a drone in the Blockly editor, one arm: An arm narrows from 26 millimetres at the root to 16 at the tip, is rounded and extruded 10 millimetres onto the plate, and carries a round pad for the motor at its tip.
Build a drone in the Blockly editor, one arm: Six bolts hold the arm, two clamping it between the plates and four fixing the motor from below, all the M3 bolt again.
Build a drone in the Blockly editor, one arm: The motor's body is a profile revolved around its shaft, so a small function, revolved, does that for any list of points.
Build a drone in the Blockly editor, one arm: A blade is lofted through five twisted ellipses, from a thick root to a thin, swept tip.

Build a drone in the Blockly editor, arms around the frame: around makes the one arm into as many as arms says: in each draw, replace the part with a call of around, and the arm, the motor, the stator and the bolts stand around the frame.

Build a drone in the Blockly editor, canopy and electronics: The canopy is lofted through five rounded rectangles that narrow as they rise; a list of lists gives each one's height, size and corner radius, and a for each loop makes them.

Build a drone in the Blockly editor, landing gear: At the end of each leg a damper, its aluminium body revolved from a profile of twelve points by the revolved function the motor uses, and a steel spring, a pipe swept along a helix.
Build a drone in the Blockly editor, canopy and electronics: The GPS stands on a mast behind the canopy, its puck's edges rounded, and two antennas angle down and back from the bottom plate.
Build a drone in the Blockly editor, landing gear: A rubber foot is lofted through five circles, and two M3 bolts fix each leg's flange to the plate.
Build a drone in the Blockly editor, canopy and electronics: A honeycomb is traced on the canopy's sides by an async function.

Build a drone in the Blockly editor, landing gear: A leg is a carbon tube bent twice on its way down: a polyline whose corners are filleted, with a circle swept along it, and a flange and a boss that pass through the leg opening.
Build a drone in the Blockly editor, arms around the frame: The lights repeat too.
Build a drone in the Blockly editor, canopy and electronics: A hatch closes the top, with the bitbybit logo in it.

Build a drone in the Blockly editor, around, bolts and standoffs: Arms, motors, propellers, legs and standoffs all stand evenly around the drone, so one function, around, repeats a shape count times around the upright axis.
Build a drone in the Blockly editor, payload and sizes: The payload hangs under the frame: a camera on its gimbal at the front, its lens in glass, and the battery in two straps.

Build a drone in the Blockly editor, sizes, stage and the frame: The frame plate is a function too: a rounded rectangle, 96 by 150 millimetres, made into a face and extruded 3 millimetres, with hexagon vents from a grid cut through it at the front and the back.
Build a drone in the Blockly editor, arms around the frame: Neighbouring propellers turn opposite ways, so the drone does not spin.

Build a drone in the Blockly editor, payload and sizes: Change one number: with six arms the drone rebuilds, everything around repeats follows, and the propeller shrinks to fit between its neighbours.
Build a drone in the Blockly editor, sizes, stage and the frame: Four variables size the whole drone: the arms, how long they are, the propeller's diameter and the legs.

Build a drone in the Blockly editor, sizes, stage and the frame: Set the stage before the first part: a dark background, a city environment that metal reflects with its picture hidden, a sun that casts shadows, and the camera placed outside the drone, far enough to see all of it.

Build a drone in the Blockly editor, around, bolts and standoffs: An M3 bolt is a profile of eight points revolved into its body, with a hexagon socket cut into its head; the standoffs, the arms and the legs all use it.

Accordion, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. A group that opens and closes on its title, so a long panel stays short.
Add to cart, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. The button that puts the configured product in the cart, with its configuration.
Button, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. A button that runs an action, such as showing a part up close or resetting the view.
Camera controls, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. Buttons and sliders that zoom and turn the view, for shoppers who would rather not drag.
Checkbox, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. Any number of choices from a list, each with its own price when it has one.
Colour, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. Any colour the shopper picks, for a part that can be painted freely.
Date, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. A day picked from a calendar, such as a delivery date.
Buttons, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. Each option as a button in a row.
Cards, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. Each option as a card with its picture, name, description and price.
Dropdown cards, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. A dropdown whose options open as cards.
Dropdown images, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. A dropdown whose options open as pictures.
Images, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. Each option as a picture.
Dropdown list, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. A dropdown whose options open as a list with their prices.
Pills, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. Each option as a small rounded label, for short names.
Swatches, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. Each option as a colour, shown beside the choice's name.
Divider, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. A line, or empty space, between two parts of the panel.
Download PDF, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. A button that downloads a summary of the configuration as a PDF.
Dropdown, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. One choice from a list that opens on a click. It takes the least room, so it suits long lists.
Email, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. An email address, checked as the shopper types it.
File, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. A file the shopper uploads, such as their own artwork for a decal.
Custom HTML, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. Markup of your own, cleaned of anything that could run, with its own styles.
Image, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. A picture with an optional caption.
Link, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. A link to another page, as text or as a button.
Message, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. A notice in one of four colours: information, a warning, a success or an error.
Number, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. A number typed or stepped with the arrows, between a minimum and a maximum.
Parts list, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. What the configured product is made of, part by part with quantities, live as the shopper chooses.
Price, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. The price of the configuration as it stands, with its breakdown if you show one.
Quantity, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. How many of the configured product the shopper buys.
Radio, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. One choice, every option in view. Drawn as plain text by default, or in any of the displays below.
Range, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. A number picked with a slider, between a minimum and a maximum, in steps.
Row, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. Lays what it holds side by side, wrapping onto a new line when there is no room.
Section, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. A group with a heading and an optional description; what it holds is laid out one under the other.
Switch, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. On or off, for one feature a shopper adds or leaves out.
Tabs, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. Several groups under one strip of tabs, one shown at a time.
Text, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. A line of the shopper's own words, such as a name to print or engrave.

Text, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. Words of your own, as a heading, a subheading, body text or a caption. Write a link as the label in square brackets followed by the address in round ones.
Text area, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. Several lines of text, for notes or longer wording.
Time, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. A time of day, such as a pick-up slot.
Validation summary, as the shopper's option panel draws it on the default theme. Every choice still missing or wrong, each a link to its control.

The link part selected: its name, material, colour and finish, its connectors, and its volume and mass
The link drawn realistically: brushed aluminium with reflections and a soft shadow

The fillet hubFront open after the hubs extrude was suppressed: its edges field empty, and the message under it saying the faces it named are gone

The link's side sketch open: its outline in the view, the sketch bar above it, and its pen commands, arcs written in the link's parameters
A face of the link picked: the bar beside it and the Selection panel offer what can be done with it, and the status bar names it

Build a drone, the arm module: A code component turns the length into the arm's four corner points, wide at the root and narrow at the tip; a polygon joins them, its corners are rounded, and it is extruded 10 millimetres and lifted onto the plate.
Build a drone, the arm module: Hexagonal cut-outs lighten the arm.
Build a drone, the arm module: The arm with its motor, propeller, bolts and light is a module of its own, Arm.
Build a drone, the arm module: Six bolts hold the arm: two clamp it between the plates and four fix the motor from below.
Build a drone, the arm module: The motor is a profile revolved around its shaft, with a cavity and eight cooling slots cut away and its propeller nut on top, all in one code component.
Build a drone, the arm module: A round pad at the tip carries the motor: a cylinder whose centre takes the length as its x, joined to the arm.
Build a drone, the arm module: Inside, name the ports: length and propeller in, and arm, motor, stator, propeller, bolts and light out.
Build a drone, the arm module: Each blade is lofted through five twisted ellipses, from a thick root to a thin, swept tip, in a code component that calls the same loft the graph has.
Build a drone, arms around the frame: One Arm instance takes the arm length and the fitted propeller.
Build a drone, a module that repeats: A code component works out the angles, half a step off the axes: 45, 135, 225 and 315 for four.
Build a drone, a module that repeats: Arms, motors, propellers, legs and standoffs all stand evenly around the drone.
Build a drone, a module that repeats: Go inside the module.
Build a drone, a module that repeats: The shape is repeated count times, and so is the axis to turn around, straight up.
Build a drone, a module that repeats: Rotate shapes turns each copy by its own angle around its own axis, pairing the three lists by position, and its result leaves through the module's output.
Build a drone, a module that repeats: A bolt for the standoffs: a code component revolves its profile and cuts the hexagon socket into its head.

Build a drone, canopy and electronics: The canopy is lofted through five rounded rectangles that narrow and rise; a code component makes the sections, and the loft closes them into a solid that sits on the top plate.
Build a drone, landing gear: At the end of each leg a damper.
Build a drone, canopy and electronics: The GPS stands on a mast behind the canopy, built from nodes because it is a few simple shapes: two cylinders, the puck's edges rounded, the two joined.
Build a drone, landing gear: A rubber foot is lofted through five circles, and two of the M3 bolts fix each leg's flange to the plate.
Build a drone, sliders and the frame: A propeller must not reach its neighbour or the canopy.
Build a drone, canopy and electronics: A hatch closes the top: a rounded rectangle on the canopy's crown, made into a face and extruded 1.4 millimetres.
Build a drone, sliders and the frame: Hexagon vents come from a hexagon grid.

Build a drone, canopy and electronics: A honeycomb is traced on the canopy's sides: a code component takes the loft, grows it a little, and divides each side face into hexagon wires, eight across the long sides and five across the short ones.
Build a drone, landing gear: A leg is a carbon tube bent twice on its way down, with a flange and a boss that pass through the leg opening.
Build a drone, arms around the frame: The bolts join the steel draw.
Build a drone, canopy and electronics: The bitbybit logo goes on the hatch.
Build a drone, a module that repeats: The plate's leg openings are Around's first use: a hole 6 millimetres across, 52 from the centre, repeated four times by an Around instance.
Build a drone, sliders and the frame: The frame plate starts as a rectangle, 96 by 150 millimetres, with its corners rounded.
Build a drone, payload and sliders: The payload hangs under the frame: a camera on its gimbal at the front, and the battery in two straps.
Build a drone, sliders and the frame: The top plate is the same plate, moved up 13 millimetres; one shape feeds both.
Build a drone, arms around the frame: Neighbouring propellers turn opposite ways, so the drone does not spin.
Build a drone, payload and sliders: Move the sliders: six arms rebuild the drone, every Around follows the arms slider, and the propeller shrinks to fit between its neighbours.
Build a drone, sliders and the frame: A face fills the outline, and an extrusion gives it its thickness of 3 millimetres.
Build a drone, sliders and the frame: Three number sliders hold the drone's sizes.

Build a drone, sliders and the frame: Set the stage before the first part, so every part looks as it will in the end: a dark background, a city environment that metal reflects (its picture hidden), a sun that casts shadows, and the camera placed outside the drone, far enough to see all of it.
Build a drone, a module that repeats: A standoff is a post 10 millimetres tall, 40 from the centre, with a bolt from below and a flipped bolt from above.
Build a drone, sliders and the frame: The prisms become one compound, moved to the front and to the back of the plate.
